Encore 0.7.1: gapless playback, and lyrics that can simply highlight the line being sung.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.7.1_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.7.1_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.7.1_amd64.deb` |
| Fedora 40+ and other RPM systems (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore-0.7.1-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.7.1_amd64.AppImage` |

Encore 0.5 and later update themselves to this version: they download it in
the background and install it the next time you quit, or right away with
**Restart to update**. Updating keeps your session, settings and downloads.
From 0.4 or earlier, download it from this page. Installs from the `.deb`
or `.rpm` link here instead of updating themselves.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** a fresh download asks you to choose **Open Anyway** in **System
  Settings → Privacy & Security** once. After an update, macOS asks once
  again for access to your saved session in the Keychain; choose **Always
  Allow**.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.
- **Fedora:** install with `sudo dnf install ./Encore-0.7.1-1.x86_64.rpm`.

## What's new

- **Gapless playback.** Songs that run into each other on an album, like
  The Dark Side of the Moon, now play without a break. YouTube's audio
  files carry a little silence the encoder adds at each end, about 50 ms
  at every song change; Encore now cuts it.
- **Highlight lyrics instead of filling them.** Turn off **Settings →
  Appearance → Fill lyrics as they're sung** and the current line is
  simply highlighted as a whole.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
